title: l4-go surface map
description: The declared correspondence between two L4 encodings of the same body of law, consumed by etc/go/lib/denovo-diff.mjs (the SPEC.md §8 diff oracle). Two encodings of one subject rarely share names or structure, so nothing here is inferred: every pairing is declared, and the oracle's job is to disagree with the declaration behaviourally rather than to guess it. Every path is repo-root-relative. additionalProperties is false throughout, matching etc/go/lib/subject.mjs's refuse-by-default stance.

sides.description: `left` is the reference encoding (at G2: the committed corpus). Battery slot values are written in `left`'s vocabulary; `right` declares its renames. Nothing else privileges left over right — the triage dispositions are symmetric.

slots.description: The shared fact vocabulary. A slot is one argument's worth of facts, named once and referenced by both sides' calls — this is what makes two differently-named encodings comparable at all.

note.description: Free prose for humans and the skill. No script branches on it.

generated_by.description: Absent on a hand-written map; written by the stage that deposits one.

label.description: How this encoding is named in the triage table, e.g. "corpus" / "de novo".

module.description: Repo-relative path to the .l4 module under test.

timezone.description: IANA zone, emitted as TIMEZONE IS "…" in the generated probe. TIMEZONE is per-document and is NOT inherited through IMPORT, so an unpinned RULES EFFECTIVE DATE read inside the module fails at evaluation without it. Use the same zone the module itself declares.

stage.description: Extra repo-relative .l4 files to copy alongside the module into its scratch side-directory, for IMPORTs the sibling scan would miss. The oracle already copies every *.l4 in the module's own directory.

type.description: The L4 type of this argument IN THIS MODULE, spelled exactly as it appears after IS A / IS AN (e.g. `IssuerProfile`, `NUMBER`, `DATE`). The oracle needs it because JSONDECODE is driven by the declared result type, not by inference from the application site: without an explicit GIVETH the decode returns NOTHING. A wrong type name is loud — the generated probe fails `l4 check` naming the file and line.

rename.description: canonical field name (as written in the battery, i.e. `left`'s vocabulary) -> this module's field name. Fields not listed pass through unchanged. A field this module declares but the battery does not supply is loud: the decoder reports `Missing required field`.

kind.description: `record` slots hold an object of field->value; the rest hold a scalar. Dates are ISO-8601 strings; JSONDECODE parses them into DATE.

from_case.description: Key in a seed case's context object to draw this slot's value from (see battery.cases). Absent = this slot is supplied only by battery.rows.

perturb.description: Set false to freeze a slot — it still varies across seed rows, but the oracle generates no single-field mutations inside it.

thresholds.description: field name -> extra values the perturbation generator must try for that field. This is where a human puts the statutory boundary figures the generator cannot know. Each is also tried at ±1 for numbers.

battery.description: Where the fact battery comes from. Both sources may be used together; `rows` are appended after `cases`.

cases.description: Repo-relative path to a cases file with a top-level `cases` array, each entry {name, context}. The subject sidecar's legs['p7-dmn'].cases is the intended value: its context keys are DMN-sanitised, and the oracle un-sanitises them against the type dictionary it reads back out of `l4 render --format json --include-unused`. A key that does not un-sanitise onto a declared field is a hard error, never a silent drop.

slots.description: slot name -> value, in `left`'s field vocabulary.

rule_date.description: ISO date. When present, every pair whose rule_date is "case" is evaluated under EVAL UNDER RULES EFFECTIVE AT this date.

perturbation.description: Systematic single-field mutation of each seed row. One field at a time is what makes a divergence witness minimal by construction: the witness is `seed row + this one change`, and the seed agreed.

numeric_deltas.description: Absolute offsets applied to every numeric leaf. Default [-1, 1] — the boundary bias: a threshold is crossed by one, not by an order of magnitude.

cross_pollinate.description: For each leaf, also try every distinct value that leaf takes across the OTHER seed rows (and, for numbers, ±1 around each). The seed cases carry the regime boundaries a human already found; this reuses them everywhere instead of only where they were written.

id.description: Stable, unique. Cited by the triage table and by fork-register entries.

rule_date.description: "case" = take it from the row; an ISO date = pin it for every row; absent/null = evaluate with no EVAL UNDER RULES EFFECTIVE AT wrapper, which requires the module's own TIMEZONE.

fork.description: Optional id of a fork-register entry this pair is known to interpret. Carried into the triage table so a divergence lands next to an ambiguity somebody already recorded.

citation.description: The source-text coordinate both sides claim to encode, e.g. "17 CFR 227.100(b)".

call.description: The decision's name in this module, spelled exactly as declared (backticks are added by the oracle; do not write them). Checked against the module's own rule headings, read back from `l4 render --format json --include-unused`; a name that is not there is a hard error listing the nearest matches.

args.description: Slot names, in call order. The two sides need not have the same arity — an Interpretation parameter on one side only is expected (SPEC.md R4) — they need only agree on the answer.

field.description: Optional field to project out of a record-shaped result, so two encodings with different result records can still be compared on one answer. Absent = compare the whole rendered value.
